paper.title: A Multi-Armed Bandit Approach for Online Expert Selection in Markov Decision Processes

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-armed bandit approach to choosing experts in MDPs
unmapped: Arms are N expert stationary policies acting on a shared finite (partially observed) MDP; pulling an arm runs the expert for T_n MDP steps and observes the average reward
Markov chain induced by each expert is irreducible and aperiodic with mixing constants C_e, alpha_e
Arm 'means' are steady-state average rewards of the experts' stationary distributions; state is shared across arms (not restless/rested independent chains)
UCB algorithm requires knowledge of mixing constants K_e = C_e/(1-alpha_e) and block lengths T_n >= T_0
settings.definition_quote: We define the best expert as $e^* =\arg\max_{e \in \Ec} \bar R^e$ ... The cumulative regret, $r(n)$ after $n$ iterations of a multi-armed bandit algorithm is defined as: \[r(n)=n\bar R^* -  \sum_{k = 0}^{n}\frac{1}{T_k}\sum_{t=t_k}^{t_{k+1}-1} r_t\]

algorithms.name: Upper Confidence Bounds for MDPs (UCB with mixing-corrected confidence bounds)
Any multi-armed bandit algorithm within the MAB approach to MDPs (Algorithm 1)

symbols.N_i: E[T_e(n)], expected number of iterations expert i is chosen up to iteration n
symbols.C_i: mixing constant C_e of the Markov chain induced by expert i
symbols.alpha_i: mixing rate alpha_e of expert i's chain
symbols.C_star: mixing constant of the best expert
symbols.alpha_star: mixing rate of the best expert
symbols.T_0: lower bound on all block lengths T_n
symbols.Delta_i: bar R^* - bar R^e, steady-state reward gap

conditions: induced Markov chains of each expert are irreducible and aperiodic

source.label: prop:rdi
source.quote: If the induced Markov chains for each expert $e \in \Ec$ are irreducible and aperiodic, then the expected cumulative regret at time $n$ can be bounded with: \E[r(n)]\le \sum_{e \ne e^*} \E[ T_e(n) ] \left[ \Delta_e + \frac{C_e}{T_0(1 -\alpha_e)} \right] + \frac{C_{*}}{1-\alpha_{*}}\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \frac{1}{T_k}

results.notes: Regret decomposition identity holding for any bandit algorithm; n (bandit iterations) not appearing explicitly. Regret is n*R̄* minus realized average block rewards; mapped to pseudo_regret but comparator is the steady-state reward rather than an i.i.d. mean.

symbols.K_i: K_e = C_e/(1-alpha_e), mixing constant term of expert i
symbols.T_n: block length (MDP steps) at bandit iteration n
symbols.Delta_i: bar R^* - bar R^e, steady-state reward gap

conditions: induced Markov chains of each expert are irreducible and aperiodic
Delta_e > 2 K_e / T_0 for all suboptimal experts e
tuning: confidence bound c_{k,n}^e = K_e/T_0 + sqrt(8 log(n)/k)

source.label: prop:ucbregret
source.quote: For a set of experts $\Ec$ and initial time horizon $T_0$ such that $\bar{R^*}-\bar{R}^e > \frac{2K_e}{T_0}$ for all $e \in \Ec$, and for a choice of $\delta(n)=n^{-4}$, the expected regret of the UCB algorithm after $n$ time steps of the algorithm, $\E[r(n)]$, satisfies: ...

results.notes: T here is the paper's n = number of bandit iterations (not MDP time steps). Paper subsequently (in text) chooses T_n = T_0 + c n giving H_sum <= (1/c) log((T_0+cn-c)/T_0) and O(log n) regret; not a separate formal statement. Quantity mapping as in r1.
